Note that [(8.112)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq214) is of the same flavor as [(8.16)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq31), which is inherited to the proximal operator from its more primitive ancestor. In the sequel, we will make use of these properties to touch upon the algorithmic front, where our main interest lies.

Lemma 8.3

*Consider the convex function*

*f* : ℝ^(*l*) ↦ ℝ ∪ { + ∞}<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟼</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi><mml:mo>∪</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">{</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mo>∞</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">}</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si517.png)

*and its proximal operator* *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si518.png) *of index λ. Then the fixed point set of the proximal operator coincides with the set of minimizers of f, that is,*

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/fx041.jpg)(8.112) 

Proof

The definition of the fixed point set has been given in Section [8.3.1](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#s0035). We first assume that a point ***x*** belongs to the fixed point set, hence the action of the proximal operator leaves it unaffected, that is,

**x** = *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**),<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si519.png)

and making use of [(8.111)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq213), we get

⟨**y** − **x**, **x** − **x**⟩ ≤ *λ*(*f*(**y**)−*f*(**x**)), ∀**y** ∈ ℝ^(*l*),<mml:math><mml:mo stretchy="false">〈</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">〉</mml:mo><mml:mo>≤</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="1em"/><mml:mo>∀</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si520.png)(8.113) 

which results in

*f*(**x**) ≤ *f*(**y**), ∀**y** ∈ ℝ^(*l*).<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>≤</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="1em"/><mml:mo>∀</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si521.png)(8.114) 

That is, ***x*** is a minimizer of *f*. For the converse, we assume that ***x*** is a minimizer. Then [(8.115)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq219) is valid, from which [(8.114)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq218) is deduced, and since this is a necessary and sufficient condition for a point to be equal to the value of the proximal operator, we have proved the claim. □

Finally, note that *f* and *e*[*λ**f*]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>e</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si522.png) share the same set of minimizers. Thus, one can minimize a nonsmooth convex function by dealing with an equivalent smooth one. From a practical point of view, the value of the method depends on how easy it is to obtain the proximal operator. For example, we have already seen that if the goal is to minimize the ℓ[1]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>ℓ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si17.png) norm, the proximal operator is a simple soft thresholding operation. Needless to say that life is not always that generous!

### 8.13.2 Proximal minimization

In this section, we will exploit our experience from Section [8.4](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#s0040) to develop iterative schemes which asymptotically land their estimates in the fixed point set of the respective operator. All that is required is for the operator to own a nonexpansiveness property.

Proposition 8.6

*The proximal operator associated with a convex function is nonexpansive, that is,*

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/fx042.jpg)(8.115) 

Proof

The proof is readily obtained as a combination of the property in [(8.112)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq214) with the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. Moreover, it can be shown that the relaxed version of the proximal operator (also known as the *reflected* version),

*R*[*λ**f*](**x**) :  = 2*P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**) − *I*,<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si523.png)(8.116) 

is also nonexpansive with the same fixed point set as that of the proximal operator (Problem [8.36](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#o0210)). □

Proposition 8.7

*Let*

*f* : ℝ^(*l*) ↦ ℝ ∪ { + ∞}<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟼</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi><mml:mo>∪</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">{</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mo>∞</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">}</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si517.png)

*be a convex function, with* *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si518.png) *being the respective proximal operator of index λ. Then, starting from an arbitrary point,* **x**[0] ∈ ℝ^(*l*)<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si524.png)*, the iterative algorithm*

**x**[*k*] = **x**[*k* − 1] + *μ*[*k*](*P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**[*k* − 1])−**x**[*k* − 1]),<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si525.png)(8.117) 

*where* *μ*[*k*] ∈ (0, 2)<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si526.png) *is such that*

$\\sum\\limits\_{k = 1}^{\\infty}\\mu\_{k}(2 - \\mu\_{k}) = + \\infty,$<mml:math><mml:munderover><mml:mo movablelimits="false">∑</mml:mo><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>∞</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:munderover><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mo>∞</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si527.png)

*converges to an element of the fixed point set of the proximal operator; that is, it converges to a minimizer of f.*

The proof of the proposition is given in Problem [8.36](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#o0210) \[84\]. Observe that Eq. [(8.118)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq223) is the counterpart of Eq. [(8.26)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq56). A special case occurs if *μ*[*k*] = 1<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si528.png), which results in

**x**[*k*] = *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**[*k* − 1]),<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si529.png)(8.118) 

also known as the *proximal point* algorithm. Proximal minimization algorithms are traced back to the early 1970s \[57,72\].

Example 8.11

Let us demonstrate the previous findings via the familiar optimization task of the quadratic function

$f(\\mathbf{x}) = \\frac{1}{2}\\mathbf{x}^{T}A\\mathbf{x} - \\mathbf{b}^{T}\\mathbf{x}.$<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>T</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>T</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si530.png)

It does not take long to see that the minimizer occurs at the solution of the linear system of equations

*A***x**[\*] = **b**.<mml:math><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si531.png)

From the definition in Eq. [(8.106)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq200), taking the gradient of the quadratic function and equating to zero, we readily obtain

${Prox}\_{\\lambda f}(\\mathbf{x}) = \\left( A + \\frac{1}{\\lambda}I \\right)^{- 1}\\left( \\mathbf{b} + \\frac{1}{\\lambda}\\mathbf{x} \\right),$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si532.png)(8.119) 

and setting $\\epsilon = \\frac{1}{\\lambda}$<mml:math><mml:mi>ϵ</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si533.png), the recursion in Eq. [(8.119)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq225) becomes

**x**[*k*] = (*A*+*ϵ**I*)^( − 1)(**b** + *ϵ***x**[*k* − 1]).<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>ϵ</mml:mi><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>ϵ</mml:mi><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si534.png)(8.120) 

After some simple algebraic manipulations (Problem [8.37](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#o0215)), we finally obtain

**x**[*k*] = **x**[*k* − 1] + (*A*+*ϵ**I*)^( − 1)(**b**−*A***x**[*k* − 1]).<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>ϵ</mml:mi><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si535.png)(8.121) 

This scheme is known from the numerical linear algebra as *iterative refinement* algorithm \[58\]. It is used when the matrix *A* is near-singular, so the regularization via *ϵ* helps the inversion. Note that at each iteration, **b** − *A***x**[*k* − 1]<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si536.png) is the error committed by the current estimate. The algorithm belongs to a larger family of algorithms, known as stationary iterative or iterative relaxation schemes; we will meet such schemes in Chapter [10](#Chp010_463-518_B9780443292385000160.xhtml).

The interesting point here is that since the algorithm results as a special case of the proximal minimization algorithm, convergence to the solution is guaranteed even if *ϵ* is not small!

#### Resolvent of the subdifferential mapping

We will look at the proximal operator from a slightly different viewpoint, which will be useful to us soon, when it will be used for the solution of more general minimization tasks. We will follow a more descriptive and less mathematically formal path.

According to [Lemma 8.2](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#enun0180) and since the proximal operator is a minimizer of Eq. [(8.106)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq200), it must be chosen so that

$0 \\in \\ \\partial f(\\mathbf{v}) + \\frac{1}{\\lambda}\\mathbf{v} - \\frac{1}{\\lambda}\\mathbf{x},$<mml:math><mml:mn mathvariant="bold">0</mml:mn><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si537.png)(8.122) 

or

0∈ *λ*∂*f*(**v**) + **v** − **x**,<mml:math><mml:mn mathvariant="bold">0</mml:mn><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si538.png)(8.123) 

or

**x**∈ *λ*∂*f*(**v**) + **v**.<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si539.png)(8.124) 

Let us now define the mapping

(*I*+*λ*∂*f*) : ℝ^(*l*) ↦ ℝ^(*l*),<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟼</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si540.png)(8.125) 

such that

(*I*+*λ*∂*f*)(**v**) = **v** + *λ*∂*f*(**v**).<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si541.png)(8.126) 

Note that this mapping is one-to-many, due to the definition of the subdifferential, which is a set.^([^(58)](#fn58))

(*I*+*λ*∂*f*)^( − 1) : ℝ^(*l*) ↦ ℝ^(*l*),<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟼</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si542.png)(8.127) 

is single-valued, and as a matter of fact it coincides with the proximal operator; this is readily deduced from [(8.125)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq233), which can equivalently be written as

**x**∈ (*I*+*λ*∂*f*)(**v**),<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si543.png)

which implies that

(*I*+*λ*∂*f*)^( − 1)(**x**) = **v** = *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**).<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si544.png)(8.128) 

However, we know that the proximal operator is unique. The operator in [(8.128)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq236) is known as the *resolvent of the subdifferential mapping* \[72\].

As an exercise, let us now apply Eq. [(8.129)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq238) to the case of [Example 8.11](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#enun0295). For this case, the subdifferential set is a singleton comprising the gradient vector,

*P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**) = (*I* + *λ*∇*f*)^( − 1)(**x**) ⇒ (*I* + *λ*∇*f*)(*P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**)) = **x**,<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟹</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si545.png)

or by definition of the mapping (*I* + *λ*∇*f*)<mml:math><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si546.png) and taking the gradient of the quadratic function,

*P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**) + *λ*∇*f*(*P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**)) = *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**) + *λ**A**P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**) − *λ***b** = **x**,<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si547.png)

which finally results in

${Prox}\_{\\lambda f}(\\mathbf{x}) = \\left( A + \\frac{1}{\\lambda}I \\right)^{- 1}\\left( \\mathbf{b} + \\frac{1}{\\lambda}\\mathbf{x} \\right).$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">b</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si548.png)

## 8.14 Proximal splitting methods for optimization

A number of optimization tasks often come in the form of a summation of individual convex functions, some of them being differentiable and some of them nonsmooth. Sparsity-aware learning tasks are typical examples that have received a lot of attention, where the regularizing term is nonsmooth, for example, the ℓ[1]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>ℓ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si17.png) norm.

Our goal in this section is to solve the following minimization task:

$\\mathbf{x}\_{\\ast} = \\arg\\min\\limits\_{\\mathbf{x}}\\left\\{ f(\\mathbf{x}) + g(\\mathbf{x}) \\right\\},$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">arg</mml:mi><mml:mo>⁡</mml:mo><mml:munder><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">min</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:munder><mml:mo>⁡</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">{</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">}</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si549.png)(8.129) 

where both involved functions are convex,

*f* : ℝ^(*l*) ↦ ℝ ∪ { + ∞}, *g* : ℝ^(*l*) ↦ ℝ,<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟼</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi><mml:mo>∪</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">{</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mo>∞</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">}</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="1em"/><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟼</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si550.png)

and *g* is assumed to be differentiable while *f* is nonsmooth. It turns out that the iterative scheme

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/fx043.jpg)(8.130) 

converges to a minimizer of the sum of the involved functions, that is,

$\\mathbf{x}\_{k}\\longrightarrow\\arg\\min\\limits\_{\\mathbf{x}}\\left\\{ f(\\mathbf{x}) + g(\\mathbf{x}) \\right\\},$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟶</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">arg</mml:mi><mml:mo>⁡</mml:mo><mml:munder><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">min</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:munder><mml:mo>⁡</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">{</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">}</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si551.png)(8.131) 

for a properly chosen sequence, *λ*[*k*]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si552.png), and provided that the gradient is continuous Lipschitz, that is,

||∇*g*(**x**) − ∇*g*(**y**)|| ≤ *γ*||**x** − **y**||,<mml:math><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo>≤</mml:mo><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si553.png)(8.132) 

for some *γ* > 0<mml:math><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">&gt;</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si327.png). It can be shown that if $\\lambda\_{k} \\in \\left( 0,\\frac{1}{\\gamma} \\right\\rbrack$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="3.8ex" minsize="3.8ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="3.8ex" minsize="3.8ex">\]</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si554.png), then the algorithm converges to a minimizer at a sublinear rate, 𝒪(1/*k*)<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="script">O</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo stretchy="false">/</mml:mo><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si555.png) \[8\]. This family of algorithms is known as *proximal gradient* or *forward-backward splitting* algorithms. The term *splitting* is inherited from the split of the function into two (or more generally into more) parts. The term *proximal* indicates the presence of the proximal operator of *f* in the optimization scheme. The iteration involves an (explicit) forward gradient computation step performed on the smooth part and an (implicit) backward step via the use of the proximal operator of the nonsmooth part. The terms *forward-backward* are borrowed from numerical analysis methods involving discretization techniques \[97\]. Proximal gradient schemes are traced back to, for example, \[18,54\], but their spread in machine learning and signal processing matured later \[26,36\].

There are a number of variants of the previous basic scheme. A version that achieves an $\\mathcal{O}(\\frac{1}{k^{2}})$<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="script">O</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si556.png) rate of convergence is based on the classical Nesterov modification of the gradient algorithm \[65\], and it is summarized in [Algorithm 8.5](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#enun0300) \[8\]. In the algorithm, the update is split into two parts. In the proximal operator, one uses a smoother version of the obtained estimates, using an averaging that involves previous estimates.

Algorithm 8.5

**Fast proximal gradient splitting algorithm**

*   •  Initialization 
    1.  –  Select **x**[0]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si141.png), **z**[1] = **x**[0]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si557.png), *t*[1] = 1<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>t</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si558.png).
    2.  –  Select *λ*.
*   •  **For** *k* = 1, 2, …<mml:math><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mo>…</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si559.png), **Do** 
    1.  –  **y**[*k*] = **z**[*k*] − *λ*∇*g*(**z**[*k*])<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si560.png)
    2.  –  **x**[*k*] = *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**y**[*k*])<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si561.png)
    3.  –  $t\_{k + 1} = \\frac{1 + \\sqrt{4t\_{k}^{2} + 1}}{2}$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>t</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:msqrt><mml:mrow><mml:mn>4</mml:mn><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>t</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msqrt></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si562.png)
    4.  –  $\\mu\_{k} = \\frac{t\_{k} - 1}{t\_{k + 1}}$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>t</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>t</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si563.png)
    5.  –  **z**[*k* + 1] = **x**[*k*] + *μ*[*k*](**x**[*k*] − **x**[*k* − 1])<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si564.png)
*   •  **End For**

Note that the algorithm involves a step size *μ*[*k*]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si334.png). The computation of the variables *t*[*k*]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>t</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si565.png) is done in such a way that convergence speed is optimized. However, it has to be noted that convergence of the scheme is no more guaranteed, in general.

### The proximal forward-backward splitting operator

From a first look, the iterative update given in Eq. [(8.131)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq244) seems to be a bit “magic.” However, this is not the case and we can come to it by following simple arguments starting from the basic property of a minimizer. Indeed, let **x**[\*]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si40.png) be a minimizer of Eq. [(8.130)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq242). Then we know that it has to satisfy

0 ∈ ∂*f*(**x**[\*]) + ∇*g*(**x**[\*]), or equivalently0 ∈ *λ*∂*f*(**x**[\*]) + *λ*∇*g*(**x**[\*]), or equivalently0 ∈ *λ*∂*f*(**x**[\*]) + **x**[\*] − **x**[\*] + *λ*∇*g*(**x**[\*]),<mml:math><mml:mn mathvariant="bold" id="mmlbr0016">0</mml:mn><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mtext>or equivalently</mml:mtext><mml:mspace linebreak="newline"/><mml:mn mathvariant="bold">0</mml:mn><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mtext>or equivalently</mml:mtext><mml:mspace linebreak="newline"/><mml:mn mathvariant="bold">0</mml:mn><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si566.png)

or equivalently

(*I*−*λ*∇*g*)(**x**[\*]) ∈ (*I*+*λ*∂*f*)(**x**[\*]),<mml:math><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si567.png)

or

(*I*+*λ*∂*f*)^( − 1)(*I*−*λ*∇*g*)(**x**[\*]) = **x**[\*],<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si568.png)

and finally

**x**[\*] = *P**r**o**x*[*λ**f*](**x**[\*]−*λ*∇*g*(**x**[\*])).<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Prox</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>⁎</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si569.png)(8.133) 

In other words, a minimizer of the task is a fixed point of the operator

(*I*+*λ*∂*f*)^( − 1)(*I*−*λ*∇*g*) : ℝ^(*l*) ↦ ℝ^(*l*).<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∂</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mi>I</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">∇</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="2.4ex" minsize="2.4ex">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">⟼</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>l</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si570.png)(8.134) 

The latter is known as the *proximal forward-backward splitting operator* and it can be shown that if $\\lambda \\in \\left( 0,\\frac{1}{\\gamma} \\right\\rbrack$<mml:math><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo>∈</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="3.8ex" minsize="3.8ex">(</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="true" maxsize="3.8ex" minsize="3.8ex">\]</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si571.png), where *γ* is the Lipschitz constant, then this operator is *nonexpansive* \[108\]. This short story justifies the reason that the iteration in Eq. [(8.131)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq244) is attracted toward the set of minimizers.

Remarks 8.10

*   •  The proximal gradient splitting algorithm can be considered as a generalization of some previously considered algorithms. If we set *f*(**x**) = *ι*[*C*](**x**)<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>ι</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>C</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si572.png), the proximal operator becomes the projection operator and the projected gradient algorithm of Eq. [(8.62)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq128) results. If *f*(**x**) = 0<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si573.png), we obtain the gradient algorithm and if *g*(**x**) = 0<mml:math><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si574.png) the proximal point algorithm comes up.
*   •  Besides batch proximal splitting algorithms, online schemes have been proposed (see \[36,48,106,107\]), with an emphasis on the ℓ[1]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>ℓ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si17.png) regularization tasks.
*   •  The literature on the application and the development of novel versions of this family of algorithms in the fields of machine learning and signal processing is very rich, and the interested reader can delve deeper into the field via, e.g., \[7,28,67,108\].

### Alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)

Extensions of the proximal splitting gradient algorithm for the case where both functions *f* and *g* are nonsmooth have also been developed, such as the *Douglas–Rachford* algorithm \[27,54\]. Here, we are going to focus on one of the most popular schemes, known as the *alternating direction method of multipliers* (ADMM) algorithm \[40\].

The ADMM algorithm is based on the notion of the *augmented Lagrangian* and at its very heart lies the Lagrangian duality concept (Appendix C).

The goal is to minimize the sum *f*(**x**) + *g*(**x**)<mml:math><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si575.png), where both *f* and *g* can be nonsmooth. This equivalently can be written as

minimize with respect to **x**, **y**    *f*(**x**) + *g*(**y**),<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mtext>minimize with respect to </mml:mtext><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si576.png)(8.135) 

subject to    **x** − **y** = 0.<mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mtext>subject to</mml:mtext><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mspace width="0.25em"/><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn mathvariant="bold">0</mml:mn><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si577.png)(8.136) 

The augmented Lagrangian is defined as

$L\_{\\lambda}(\\mathbf{x},\\mathbf{y},\\mathbf{z}): = f(\\mathbf{x}) + g(\\mathbf{y}) + \\frac{1}{\\lambda}\\mathbf{z}^{T}(\\mathbf{x} - \\mathbf{y}) + \\frac{1}{2\\lambda}||\\mathbf{x} - \\mathbf{y}||^{2},$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>T</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si578.png)(8.137) 

where we have denoted the corresponding Lagrange multipliers^([^(59)](#fn59))

$L\_{\\lambda}(\\mathbf{x},\\mathbf{y},\\mathbf{z}): = f(\\mathbf{x}) + g(\\mathbf{y}) + \\frac{1}{2\\lambda}||\\mathbf{x} - \\mathbf{y} + \\mathbf{z}||^{2} - \\frac{1}{2\\lambda}||\\mathbf{z}||^{2}.$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi>f</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>g</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>.</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si579.png)(8.138) 

The ADMM is given in [Algorithm 8.6](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#enun0310).

Algorithm 8.6

**The ADMM algorithm**

*   •  Initialization 
    1.  –  Fix *λ* > 0<mml:math><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">&gt;</mml:mo><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si486.png).
    2.  –  Select **y**[0], **z**[0]<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>0</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si580.png).
*   •  **For** *k* = 1, 2, …<mml:math><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mo>…</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si559.png), **Do** 
    1.  –  **x**[*k*] = prox[*λ**f*](**y**[*k* − 1] − **z**[*k* − 1])<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mtext>prox</mml:mtext></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>f</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si581.png)
    2.  –  **y**[*k*] = prox[*λ**g*](**x**[*k*] + **z**[*k* − 1])<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mtext>prox</mml:mtext></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mi>g</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si582.png)
    3.  –  **z**[*k*] = **z**[*k* − 1] + (**x**[*k*] − **y**[*k*])<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>k</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si583.png)
*   •  **End For**

Looking carefully at the algorithm and Eq. [(8.139)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq255), observe that the first recursion corresponds to the minimization of the augmented Lagrangian with respect to ***x***, keeping ***y*** and ***z*** fixed from the previous iteration. The second recursion corresponds to the minimization with respect to ***y***, by keeping ***x*** and ***z*** frozen to their currently available estimates. The last iteration is an update of the *dual* variables (Lagrange multipliers) in the *ascent* direction; note that the difference in the parentheses is the gradient of the augmented Lagrangian with respect to ***z***. Recall from Appendix C that the saddle point is found via a max-min problem of the primal (**x**, **y**)<mml:math><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si584.png) and the dual variables. The convergence of the algorithm has been analyzed in \[40\]. For related tutorial papers the reader can look at, e.g., \[16,46\].

### Mirror descent algorithms

A closely related algorithmic family to the forward-backward optimization algorithms is traced back to the work in \[64\]; it is known as *mirror descent algorithms* (MDAs). The method has undergone a number of evolutionary steps (for example, \[9,66\]). Our focus will be on adopting online schemes to minimize the regularized expected loss function

*J*(**θ**) = 𝔼 \[ℒ(**θ**,*y*,**x**)\] + *ϕ*(**θ**),<mml:math><mml:mi>J</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mml:mi><mml:mspace width="0.2em"/><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">\[</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">y</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold">x</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true">\]</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>ϕ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si585.png)

where the regularizing function, *ϕ*, is assumed to be convex, but not necessarily smooth. In a more recent representative of this algorithmic class, also known as *regularized dual averaging* (RDA) algorithm \[100\], the main iterative equation is expressed as

$\\mathbf{\\theta}\_{n} = \\text{arg}\\min\\limits\_{\\mathbf{\\theta}}\\left\\{ \\langle{\\overline{\\mathcal{L}}}^{\\prime},\\mathbf{\\theta}\\rangle + \\phi(\\mathbf{\\theta}) + \\mu\_{n}\\psi(\\mathbf{\\theta}) \\right\\},$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mtext>arg</mml:mtext><mml:munder><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">min</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:munder><mml:mo>⁡</mml:mo><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">{</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">〈</mml:mo><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mover accent="true"><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">¯</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>′</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">〉</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:mi>ϕ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mi>ψ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="true">}</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si586.png)(8.139) 

where *ψ* is a *strongly convex* auxiliary function. For example, one possibility is to choose *ϕ*(**θ**) = *λ*||**θ**||[1]<mml:math><mml:mi>ϕ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi>λ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msub></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si587.png) and *ψ*(**θ**) = ||**θ**||[2]²<mml:math><mml:mi>ψ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">|</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si588.png) \[100\]. The average subgradient of ℒ<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si191.png) up to and including time instant *n* − 1<mml:math><mml:mi>n</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si412.png) is denoted by ${\\overline{\\mathcal{L}}}^{\\prime}$<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mover accent="true"><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">¯</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>′</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si589.png), that is,

${\\overline{\\mathcal{L}}}^{\\prime} = \\frac{1}{n - 1}\\sum\\limits\_{j = 1}^{n - 1}\\mathcal{L}\_{j}^{\\prime}(\\mathbf{\\theta}\_{j}),$<mml:math><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mover accent="true"><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="false">¯</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:mover></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>′</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:munderover><mml:mo movablelimits="false">∑</mml:mo><mml:mrow><mml:mi>j</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi><mml:mo linebreak="badbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:munderover><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>j</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>′</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>j</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>,</mml:mo></mml:math>

![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si590.png)

where ℒ[*j*](**θ**) :  = ℒ(**θ**, *y*[*j*], **x**[*j*])<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>j</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo><mml:mo>:</mml:mo><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="script">L</mml:mi><mml:mo stretchy="false">(</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">θ</mml:mi><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>y</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>j</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo>,</mml:mo><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>j</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo stretchy="false">)</mml:mo></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si591.png).

It can be shown that if the subgradients are bounded, and $\\mu\_{n} = \\mathcal{O}\\left( \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{n}} \\right)$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="script">O</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:msqrt><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msqrt></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si592.png), then following regret analysis arguments an $\\mathcal{O}\\left( \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{n}} \\right)$<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="script">O</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:msqrt><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msqrt></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si593.png) convergence rate is achieved. If, on the other hand, the regularizing term is strongly convex and $\\mu\_{n} = \\mathcal{O}\\left( \\frac{\\ln n}{n} \\right)$<mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow><mml:mi>μ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:msub><mml:mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mml:mo><mml:mi mathvariant="script">O</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">ln</mml:mi><mml:mo>⁡</mml:mo><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si594.png), then an $\\mathcal{O}\\left( \\frac{\\ln n}{n} \\right)$<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="script">O</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mi mathvariant="normal">ln</mml:mi><mml:mo>⁡</mml:mo><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si595.png) rate is obtained. In \[100\], different variants are proposed. One is based on Nesterov's arguments, as used in [Algorithm 8.5](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#enun0300), which achieves an $\\mathcal{O}\\left( \\frac{1}{n^{2}} \\right)$<mml:math><mml:mi mathvariant="script">O</mml:mi><mml:mrow><mml:mo stretchy="true">(</mml:mo><mml:mfrac><mml:mrow><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>n</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:mrow></mml:mfrac><mml:mo stretchy="true">)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:math>![Equation](images/B9780443292385000147/si596.png) convergence rate.

A closer observation of Eq. [(8.140)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq257) reveals that it can be considered as a generalization of the recursion given in Eq. [(8.131)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq244). Indeed, let us set in Eq. [(8.140)](#Chp008_343-416_B9780443292385000147.xhtml#deq257)
